audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 0 and 4 read Skill while the page's own why[] text hands both stages to Tryndamere.
audit.why: whys[0]: 'Tryndamere's Fury crits and Bloodlust sustain beat your L1 pokes outright'; early: 'Tryndamere bullies the L1-2 window'. whys[4]: 'Undying Rage hard-counters your R all-in, handing him level 6'; spikes[1] says the same at length. packet.levelChart agrees — Tryndamere everywhere except levels 4-5, which it calls Skill and the page already does too.
audit.corrected: Rows 0 and 4 flipped to Tryndamere in both layers as one atomic group. EVEN 6/10 kept: Illaoi wins 51.88% on side-lane and teamfight value rather than on lane stages, which is what the late block already says.

audit.whatIsWrong: Undying Rage is described as 'Unkillable 5s' in three places, with no cooldown anywhere on the page.
audit.why: Riot's text is 'Tryndamere's lust for battle becomes so strong that he is unable to die, no matter how wounded he becomes' — no duration is given in the kit data, so the 5 seconds is not something this data supports, and it is the number the page repeats as its headline fact. What IS known is the cooldown: 120/100/80s, identical to Leap of Faith at rank 1. That is the number that decides when you can force the fight, and it was missing.
audit.corrected: The unsupported duration replaced with the real 120s at rank 1 in dosFull[0], report[5] and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Test of Spirit is called a 'tether' twice (spikes[0] 'a landed E-tether', mid 'E-tether-into-W'), and Mocking Shout does not appear anywhere on the page.
audit.why: Test of Spirit is not a tether: Riot's text is that the spirit stands in place, echoes a percentage of the damage it takes onto the champion, and 'if killed, or if the target gets too far from the spirit, the target will become a Vessel and begin spawning Tentacles'. Against Tryndamere specifically that inverts the read — his instinct is to Spinning Slash away from the spirit, and doing so turns him into a Vessel that grows your field. A player who thinks it is a tether will chase him instead of holding position. Mocking Shout (W, 14s flat, 850 range) 'decreas[es] surrounding champions' Attack Damage. Enemies with their backs turned to Tryndamere also have their Move Speed reduced' — the slow is conditional on facing away, so disengaging is what makes it work, and it saps the AD your slams scale from. Neither half was on the page.
audit.corrected: Tether language replaced with the Vessel condition in spikes[0] and mid; Mocking Shout's back-turned slow and AD sap written into report[5] and dontsFull[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown number appears on the page at all, despite the whole plan being 'trade around Undying Rage'.
audit.why: Undying Rage 120/100/80s, Spinning Slash 12/11/10/9/8s, Bloodlust 12s flat, Mocking Shout 14s flat — against Test of Spirit at 16s and Harsh Lesson at 4s. Spinning Slash at 12 seconds is the dodge that beats Test of Spirit's 16, which is why the two cooldowns matter more than his ultimate in lane.
audit.corrected: All four written into breakdown.cooldowns, with Spinning Slash's 12s also in spikes[0] and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Executioner's Calling early — his healing fights your pattern' names no heal.
audit.why: Bloodlust (Q, 12s) consumes his Fury to heal, and his AD rises as he gets more wounded — so the longer a grind runs the more he heals and the harder he hits. That is the _missing needs-antiheal flag and it makes the anti-heal a first-back item rather than a situational one.

All three suspectNames hits are false positives: 'Undying Rage' and 'Test of Spirit' are Riot's real names, and 'Build Fury' in wants.foe[0] refers to the Battle Fury resource rather than misnaming the passive.

edits.before: Tryndamere's Spinning Slash (E) plus Fury-fueled crits let him trade or dodge your Test of Spirit (E), and his passive crit chance climbs as he takes damage, so every all-in you attempt feeds his Fury bar. Your only real window is a clean W (Harsh Lesson) reposition onto a landed E-tether, but he can Q-heal (Bloodlust) most of it back.
edits.after: Tryndamere's Spinning Slash (E, 12s) plus Fury-fuelled crits let him trade or dodge your Test of Spirit, and his crit chance climbs as he takes damage, so every all-in you attempt feeds his Fury bar. Your window is a clean Harsh Lesson onto the spirit — stay near it, because if he walks away from it he becomes a Vessel and spawns your tentacles.

edits.before: L3-6 stays his: his mobility dodges your Test of Spirit and Undying Rage (R) neuters your ultimate all-in, so kills are hard to convert. The one flat patch is Levels 4-5, where a well-timed E-tether-into-W can even a trade before his R is up.
edits.after: L3-6 stays his: his 12-second Spinning Slash dodges Test of Spirit and Undying Rage neuters your ultimate all-in, so kills are hard to convert. The flat patch is Levels 4-5, where E onto him and a Harsh Lesson leap can even a trade before his R is up.

edits.before: Unkillable 5s. Wait it out, then grind him. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: He cannot die while it holds — 120s at rank 1, so fight after he spends it.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Turn your back and Mocking Shout slows you — it also saps your AD.

edits.before: Track Tryndamere's Undying Rage: Unkillable 5s. Wait it out, then grind him. When it is down — Slam him in your field.
edits.after: Undying Rage is 120s at rank 1; Mocking Shout only slows you if your back is turned, so never walk away from him.

edits.before: - Tryndamere Undying Rage: matchup-defining — Unkillable 5s. Wait it out, then grind him. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Tryndamere Undying Rage (120s at rank 1): he cannot die while it holds — fight after it. - Spinning Slash 12s is his dodge. - Bloodlust 12s heals off Fury. - Test of Spirit 16s: never on chip. - Leap of Faith: kill windows.

edits.before: Start Doran's Shield + pot. Core: Iceborn Gauntlet  (the slow makes tentacles land), then Sterak's Gage; boots Plated Steelcaps. Executioner's Calling early — his healing fights your pattern.
edits.after: Start Doran's Shield + pot. Core: Iceborn Gauntlet  (the slow makes tentacles land), then Sterak's Gage; boots Plated Steelcaps. Executioner's Calling early — Bloodlust turns Fury into health.

notes: 'Unkillable 5s' was the page's headline fact about Undying Rage and the kit data does not contain a duration for it — Riot's description says only that he is unable to die. The number may well be right from memory, but it is exactly the kind of claim the brief says to leave alone, so it was replaced with the cooldown, which is in the data. UNVERIFIED and not written: whether Undying Rage's death-prevention interacts with the damage a spirit echoes back (spikes[1] implies he simply outlives the tentacle wave), and whether it soaks turret aggro the way spikes[2] claims — neither is answerable from the kits. Standing Illaoi flag misfires unwritten as elsewhere: Leap of Faith does not ground or grant untargetability, Test of Spirit does not slow.
